;Arts and culture
*[[92nd Academy Awards]]
**The nominees for this year’s [[Academy Awards]] are announced. ''[[Joker (2019 film)|Joker]]'' receives 11 nominations, including for [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] and [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], the most out of those nominated. [https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/lists/oscar-nominations-2020-complete-list-nominees-updating-live-1267880 (''The Hollywood Reporter'')]

;Business and economy
* The [[Competition Commission of India]] launches an [[Competition law|antitrust]] probe into [[Flipkart]] and the Indian subsidy of [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]], alleging that they were promoting certain sellers at the expense of smaller merchants. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-antitrust-ecommerce/india-orders-antitrust-probe-against-amazon-walmarts-flipkart-idUSKBN1ZC1BO (Reuters)]
*[[Raphael Bostic]], President of the Federal Reserve Bank in Atlanta, says in a speech that he, as a member of the [[Federal Reserve Board]] is inclined to keep interest rates at their present, very low, levels. Any evidence of overborrowing or volatility will have to be "systemic" for him to change his mind. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-fed-bostic/fed-on-hold-but-will-financial-risks-matter-idUSKBN1ZC21E (Reuters)] 
*[[China–United States trade war]]
**The [[United States Department of the Treasury|U.S. Department of the Treasury]] de-lists [[China]] as a [[currency manipulator]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trade-china/u-s-treasury-removes-designation-of-china-as-currency-manipulator-idUSKBN1ZC2FV (Reuters)]
*[[Visa Inc.]] purchases [[financial technology]] firm [[Plaid (company)|Plaid]] for [[U.S. dollar|US$]]5.3 billion, after it and [[Mastercard]] each invested US$250 million into the company last year. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-plaid-m-a-visa/visa-to-buy-fintech-startup-plaid-in-5-3-billion-deal-idUSKBN1ZC2BF (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*A [[sinkhole]] swallows a bus and several pedestrians on a busy street in [[Xining]], [[China]], killing six people and leaving 16 others injured. According to [[state media]], the sinkhole stretches nearly 10m (32 feet) in diameter. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-china-51101683 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[Libyan peace process]]
**Representatives of Libya's [[Government of National Accord]] (GNA) and General [[Khalifa Haftar]]'s rival [[Libyan National Army]] (LNA) reach a ceasefire agreement after talks in [[Moscow]] between warring factions in Libya, also attended by Russian and Turkish officials. The preliminary agreement was signed by GNA head [[Fayez al-Sarraj]], while Haftar plans to sign it the next day. [https://www.rt.com/news/478151-lavrov-progress-ceasefire-talks/ (RT)]
*[[Saudi Arabia–United States relations]], aftermath of the [[Naval Air Station Pensacola shooting]]
**The [[United States]] expels 21 [[Royal Saudi Air Force]] cadets. Amid an investigation into the [[Saudi Arabia]]n military following the attack on [[Naval Air Station Pensacola]] in [[Florida]], the cadets were found to have [[jihadist]] material and [[child pornography]] on their phones. However, none of the cadets are believed to have assisted the gunman in the attack. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-51095771 (BBC News)]

;Law and crime
*The [[Lahore High Court]], in [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], [[Pakistan]], says the [[capital punishment in Pakistan|death sentence]] verdict against former ruler [[Pervez Musharraf]] last month is unconstitutional, casting into doubt the legitimacy of the verdict. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-law-musharraf/pakistani-judges-rule-special-court-in-musharraf-case-was-unconstitutional-idUSKBN1ZC12E (Reuters)]
*[[Murder of Ján Kuciak]]
**A suspect accepts guilt for having killed the [[investigative journalism|investigative journalist]] and his fiancée. [https://www.cbc.ca/amp/1.5424644 (CBC News)]
*[[Crime in China]]
**After a standoff, police in [[Hohhot]], [[Inner Mongolia]] shoot and kill a hostage taker who had taken three hostages with a homemade gun. The case comes less than a year after five were killed in a shooting in Inner Mongolia, and the case is under investigation. [https://www.scmp.com/news/china/society/article/3045826/chinese-police-free-three-hostages-after-killing-kidnapper-armed (''South China Morning Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]]
**[[New Jersey]] [[United States Senate|Senator]] [[Cory Booker]] drops out of the U.S. presidential race. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2020-election/cory-booker-drops-out-presidential-race-n1114426?cid=sm_npd_nn_tw_ma (NBC News)]

;Science and technology
*[[Presolar grains]]
**Analysis of a meteorite found in Australia in 1969 reveals [[Cosmic dust#stardust|stardust]] formed 5 to 7 billion years ago, older than Earth's 4.6 billion year-old sun, making the meteor and its stardust the oldest solid material ever discovered on Earth. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/technology/the-oldest-material-on-earth-has-been-found-in-a-meteorite/ar-BBYUQy4 (MSN)]
*[[Naval Air Station Pensacola shooting]]
**[[Apple Inc.|Apple]] says it is helping authorities in the [[Pensacola, Florida|Pensacola]] shooting investigation but refuses to unlock their phones. [https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/scottlucas/william-barr-apple-request-unlock-iphones (''BuzzFeed News'')] 

;Sports
* [[Houston Astros sign stealing scandal]]
** [[Houston Astros]] general manager [[Jeff Luhnow]] and manager [[A. J. Hinch]] are suspended by [[Major League Baseball]] for the entire [[2020 Major League Baseball season|2020 season]] after the league concludes its investigation into the team's illegal use of technology to [[sign stealing|steal signs]] during the team's [[2017 Houston Astros season|championship 2017 season]]. They are also fired by the organization. [https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/28476780/astros-jeff-luhnow-aj-hinch-fired-sign-stealing (ESPN)]
*[[2020 College Football Playoff National Championship]]
**In [[American football]], [[2019 LSU Tigers football team|LSU]] defeats [[2019 Clemson Tigers football team|Clemson]] to win the national championship. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/sports/lsu-smothers-clemson-42-25-seize-college-football-s-national-n1114896 (NBC News)]
